text:
Joel Eriksson Ek scored 25 seconds in, and the Minnesota Wild never let the Flames get level. The 4-1 win in Calgary was their fifth straight, their ninth in a row on the road and extended a 13-game point streak (11-0-2), as NHL.com's Heather Rule noted. At 17-3-4 and 38 points, the Wild sit on top of the NHL.

The early goals were the cheap ones. Eriksson Ek tipped one in to open it, set up by Matt Boldy and Kirill Kaprizov, and Quinn Hughes made it 2-0 at 8:09 on a wrist shot our numbers gave a 2% chance. Simon Nemec got Calgary within one late in the first, and the Flames' best stretch followed: they won the second period 1.58 to 0.33 in expected goals (the quality of the chances). That was the moment for Jesper Wallstedt. Aydar Suniev had a 33% look in the second, the best chance of the night that didn't go in, and the Flames' push came up empty.

In between, Kaprizov scored a between-the-legs power-play goal at 2:31 of the second for a 3-1 lead. He finished with a goal and two assists, giving him 11 points in his last four games, per Rule. Boldy matched him with a goal and two assists, sealing it with 49 seconds left.

Calgary had the better of the chances at even strength, 2.19 expected goals to 1.53, and replay every shot and the Flames win this game 65% of the time. Wallstedt made the difference: 22 saves on 23 shots, 1.63 goals better than expected, in a November that has turned him into one of the stories of the Wild's season. At the other end Dustin Wolf allowed three on 21 shots, 1.16 more than the chances deserved.

The Flames, playing without Kevin Bahl for the season, can take something from a game they pushed for long stretches. But they lost to a team that scored first, defended a lead and got a save every time it needed one. That's been the Wild all month.
headline: Wild win fifth straight and ninth in a row on the road
